episode_appearances.video_title: Black Paper Party Shark Tank clip — Sony Pictures Television
episode_appearances.pitch: Inclusive holiday and celebration products featuring Black characters and culture.
episode_appearances.offer: Barbara Corcoran proposed $250,000 for 20% with Mark Cuban; after negotiation Black Paper Party countered/accepted $250,000 for 10% from Barbara alone.

timeline.event: Madia Willis, Jasmine Hudson and J’Aaron Merchant launched Black Paper Party.
ABC broadcast Black Paper Party in season 15 episode 8.
Founders accepted Barbara Corcoran’s $250,000-for-10% offer on air.
CEO Madia Willis told The Philadelphia Inquirer that BPP and Corcoran’s team were still working out details before anything was official.
BLACK PAPER PARTY word mark registration 7306092 registered to Black Paper Party LLC, an Arkansas LLC.
Inc later reported 2024 revenue of $1.4 million, compared with $797,000 the prior year.
Target did not reorder Black Paper Party products; founders told AfroTech the brand ceased being shelved there.
Inc reported the founders did not close the off-camera deal with Corcoran.
Black Paper Party’s current site actively sells products.

registry_records.limitation: USPTO registration 7306092 identifies Black Paper Party LLC as an Arkansas LLC. Arkansas SOS entity filing number and current good-standing/status were not returned by the web interface; exact portal logged in search trail.

claims.text: Black Paper Party is operating as of 2026-09-09, but reputable later reporting says the $250,000-for-10% Barbara Corcoran deal accepted on air did not close off-camera.

The provisional label “Black Paper Company” is a tracker error, not a company alias. ABC’s official roster identifies the pitch as Black Paper Party in S15E8; preserve the old row only as correction provenance.

Current company retail page still advertises Target availability, while Inc and AfroTech report Target stopped carrying the brand in 2025. This is an observable current-page-versus-dated-report conflict; no archive proves when or whether that page was edited.
Later reputable reporting supersedes early headlines calling the on-air acceptance an investment: the off-camera deal did not close.

episode_appearances.offer: No Shark made an accepted investment offer; all Sharks ultimately passed.

timeline.event: Blackdot’s current investor page says the company was incorporated as a Delaware C-Corp.
Dated terms identified Blackdot, Inc. as the contracting party.
ABC broadcast Blackdot in season 16 episode 14.
Joel Pennington asked $1.5 million for 5%; the Sharks passed and he left without a deal.
USPTO published patent US 12,539,407 B2 assigned/filed by Blackdot, Inc., Austin, Texas.
Blackdot posted replacement/current terms for its Austin studio and marketplace, but the page no longer names Blackdot, Inc. as the contracting entity.
Current site offers robotic tattoo bookings/design marketplace services.

registry_records.limitation: 2023 official terms and 2026 USPTO patent identify Blackdot, Inc.; current investor page says Delaware C-Corp. Delaware registry name search is interactive and status may require paid status lookup; file number/status remain unresolved.

claims.text: Blackdot is operating as of 2026-09-09; Joel Pennington left Shark Tank without an investment, while current company pages and 2026 USPTO patent activity show continued operations under/around Blackdot, Inc.

The ABC S16E14 page body correctly lists Blackdot, but its introductory synopsis describes unrelated businesses. Treat roster/body and broadcast date as authoritative for this appearance and preserve the synopsis mismatch as a page-quality conflict.

A later verified Shark Tank Global video labels the Blackdot material “Season 16 Episode 2,” while ABC’s broadcast roster is S16E14. This is a numbering/metadata conflict, not evidence of a second televised pitch.

Blackdot’s dated 2023 terms expressly named Blackdot, Inc.; current May 2026 terms omit the legal suffix/entity name. The change is observable, but no evidence establishes why it changed or whether ownership changed.

episode_appearances.video_title: Blinger Shark Tank clip — Sony Pictures Television
episode_appearances.pitch: A reusable hair-gem styling tool and crystal system.
episode_appearances.offer: Barbara Corcoran offered $200,000 for 25% contingent on Cella coming to New York for an operational restructuring; Cella added purchase-order funding and accepted.

timeline.event: GEMC2, LLC filed a BLINGER trademark application as a Pennsylvania LLC.
ABC broadcast Blinger in season 15 episode 20.
Angie Cella accepted Barbara Corcoran’s $200,000-for-25% offer with purchase-order funding.
Inc reported that Cella had flown to New York about six months earlier to work with Corcoran on restructuring the business, providing post-show evidence beyond the televised handshake.
Shark Tank Blog update continued to describe the Barbara deal and active business.
Blinger’s current site is selling products and states that Barbara’s expertise helped the company grow.

registry_records.limitation: USPTO application records identify GEMC2, LLC as a Pennsylvania LLC, and current company patent/refund/legal pages use GEMC2, LLC. Pennsylvania file number/current standing require direct Business Filing Services access or record request.

claims.text: Blinger is operating as of 2026-09-09; Angie Cella accepted Barbara Corcoran’s $200,000-for-25% offer plus purchase-order funding, and post-show reporting/company statements strongly corroborate a continuing Barbara relationship, although executed equity documents were not obtained.

The current Blinger Shark Tank page says the company “secured a deal” and credits Barbara’s expertise; Inc’s founder interview independently establishes that Cella worked with Corcoran after filming. This is strong closing/relationship corroboration, but not a substitute for executed investment documents.

The company page calls the 2024 company “evaluation” approximately $800,000. That figure corresponds to $200,000/25% deal valuation, not the $4 million implied by the original $200,000/5% ask; the article preserves both instead of treating the later wording as the original valuation.

episode_appearances.video_title: Boona Shark Tank clip — Sony Pictures Television
episode_appearances.pitch: The Tandem Shower attachment, designed to create a dual-showerhead experience.
episode_appearances.offer: Kevin O’Leary offered $400,000 for 10% plus a $40-per-unit royalty until $1.2M was recouped, or $400,000 for 33.3%. Founders countered $600,000 for 20%; no Shark accepted.

timeline.event: Registry-derived Washington data reports Deburr LLC filed in Washington under number 604736501.
Contemporaneous reporting covered the founders’ Tandem Kickstarter/product development.
ABC says Boona released its first product, Tandem Shower, in 2023.
ABC broadcast Boona in season 15 episode 17.
Founders asked $400,000 for 10%; Kevin O’Leary made two structures; founders countered $600,000 for 20% and left without a deal.
Canadian Intellectual Property Office registered BOONA to Deburr LLC at a Seattle address, providing government-source continuity for the operator/brand relationship.
Boona’s current site actively sells Tandem Shower for $199 with a five-year guarantee; current team page lists Brett and Jeff.

registry_records.limitation: CIPO official record identifies Deburr LLC as BOONA owner at the same Seattle address. A registry-derived mirror reports WA number 604736501 and 2021-03-24 filing, but official current standing needs direct CCFS query/certificate.

claims.text: Boona is operating as of 2026-09-09 under the Tandem Shower brand/product line; founders Brett Skaloud and Jeff Feiereisen left Shark Tank without a deal, and current official pages plus trademark records support continued operation by Deburr LLC.
Boona is the brand; Deburr LLC is the legal/operator identity supported by trademark records. Tandem Shower is a product/mark, not a successor company.

A third-party transcript page is labeled 15x15 even though ABC identifies the Boona broadcast as S15E17. The transcript content names Brett/Jeff and the $400K/10% ask; ABC controls the broadcast episode number.
